label: Q3 2026 (Jul–Sep)
asOf: close of $106.13 on 6 Nov 2026; $127.74 before the report (26 Oct)
headline: Optical Communications +44% and core EPS +36%, beating guidance across the board, yet the stock is nearly 60% below its June peak: the market is repricing “AI fiber”

points.b: Optics is now half the business
points.t: Optical Communications was $2.38B, +44%, 47% of core sales; Enterprise (data center) rose 84%, with Gen AI products more than doubling, faster than GPU shipments.
This quarter it signed four multiyear, multibillion-dollar customer agreements, including Verizon and AT&T, on top of Amazon and NVIDIA. Customers share expansion costs, lowering Corning's own risk.
Solar sales rose 37% but it is still losing money, ramping slower than expected; Section 232 trade action improved pricing for US-made solar products.

reaction: Stock: closed at $126.30 on report day (27 Oct), down 1.1%, while peers (average of Amphenol and Ciena) rose about 4%, a gap of about 5 points; it then fell with the AI sector, down 12.9% on 5 Nov, and closed at $106.13 on 6 Nov, about 31% below the end-September $153.76 and 58% below the $255.69 high since June. Consensus from Newsquawk: core EPS $0.88, core sales $5.03B.

segments.title: Segments
segments.take: Almost all the growth came from Optical Communications, with Solar a second engine; Glass Innovations (phone, TV and PC glass) is shrinking.

rows.why: Enterprise rose 84% (data-center fiber and connectivity), with Gen AI products more than doubling. Net income $532M, +80%. The NVIDIA partnership expands US optical connectivity capacity tenfold.
TV panel glass and cover glass for phones and laptops. Higher memory prices are weighing on TV, PC and phone shipments; Corning outperforms end markets by adding more glass per device.
Emissions-control ceramics and auto glass; steady growth.
Hemlock polysilicon plus US-made wafers and modules. The output ramp is slower than expected and it lost $7M; the goal is a revenue stream above $3B.

segments.note: Segment sales use Corning's hedge-rate basis and sum to roughly the $5.08B of core sales; Life Sciences & Emerging is about $290M, calculated as the difference.

extras.title: Where it sits in the AI loop
extras.take: Corning is the largest supplier of data-center fiber. AI clusters need huge amounts of fiber between GPUs, racks and data centers, so more GPUs mean more fiber.

items.w: Management says Gen AI sales are growing faster than GPU shipments because each GPU needs more fiber (higher bandwidth, more cross-rack links).

A multiyear, multibillion-dollar Amazon deal, a partnership to expand NVIDIA's US capacity tenfold, and four new deals this quarter including Verizon and AT&T. Customers share expansion costs and risk.
If data-center construction slows on power and local politics, fiber demand slows with it; but telecom fiber-to-the-home and long-haul upgrades are a separate demand line.
Higher memory prices are pressuring TV, PC and phone shipments, which weighs on Glass Innovations.

extras.title: Where growth comes from
extras.take: Corning grows on optical volume plus the solar ramp; management's Springboard plan targets $40B of annualized sales by end-2030. The real variable is the pace of data-center construction.

items.w: Enterprise +84%, with capacity expansion backed by long-term agreements.
Up 3.1 points from a year ago; the plan is for profits to grow faster than sales, and ROIC was 16.7% this quarter.
Sales +37% but still loss-making; Section 232 and US manufacturing incentives improve pricing. The ramp is slower than expected.
Annualized sales of $20B by end-2026, $30B by end-2028 and $40B by end-2030, about a 19% CAGR from 2026Q4 to 2030Q4.
Slower data-center construction; new technologies such as hollow-core fiber changing volumes; continued solar losses; further declines in consumer-electronics glass.

trends.why: +36% in a year, faster than sales

valuation.take: About 34 times trailing core earnings and about 31 times 2026, with a P/S of about 5.2, twice the five-year median of 2.5. The price bets on Springboard delivering; since the report the stock has given back more than half its peak.

forward.title: Full-year 2026 from company guidance
forward.note: 2026 core sales about $19.4B (Q4 at the $5.25B midpoint), about +18% y/y.

scenarios.note: Bear: data-center construction slows and solar keeps losing money, about 4% growth over two years; base: close to Springboard's $30B annualized by end-2028 (about $26B for the year); bull: optics and solar both beat. EPS = sales × core net margin ÷ 875M shares. These assumptions are ours and are not forecasts.

pricezone.sub: 2028 core EPS × our P/E; price at the 6 Nov close
pricezone.why: The price is slightly above the zone: buying at $106, the base case gains about 12% and the bear case loses about 34%, a reward/risk of about 0.4. At the $95 midpoint it is about 1.0, and at the $85 low end about 2.3. The multiples are above Corning's usual 15–20x of the past decade, because optics is now over half the business and growth has doubled; but it is still a capital-heavy materials company, and we don't give it an AI-chip multiple.

history.title: Against its own past
history.sub: P/S (TTM GAAP sales, diluted shares), last 20 quarter ends
history.note: The multiple climbed fast from 2H 2025 to 13x at end-June 2026; it's about 5.2x now, still twice the five-year median of 2.5x. Calculated from SEC XBRL quarterly sales, diluted shares and Nasdaq quarter-end closes.

cash.title: Core EPS

stats.k: Adjusted free cash flow this quarter

cash.note: Adjusted free cash flow over the first three quarters was $2.27B, against $0.99B a year earlier. Capex was $545M (a year ago $334M), with customers sharing part of the expansion cost, so cash flow is still improving.

ret.note: The quarterly dividend is $0.28 a share, about $1.0B over the last four quarters; there were no buybacks in the first three quarters of 2026, with cash going first to expansion.

calc: Price $106.13: 6 Nov close (Nasdaq); $127.74 before the report (26 Oct), $126.30 that day (27 Oct)
Scenario EPS = sales × core net margin ÷ 875M shares; price = EPS × multiple, rounded
Reward/risk = gain to the base price ÷ loss to the bear price

changes.now: +19%, “the strongest growth since the launch of Springboard”, with Q4 guided to +19% again.

changes.before: Two big deals with Amazon and NVIDIA.
changes.now: Four more multiyear, multibillion-dollar deals this quarter, including Verizon and AT&T.

changes.before: Last quarter: profits improve from Q3.
changes.now: Sales +37% but still loss-making; the ramp is “slower than anticipated”.

items: Core sales +19% and core EPS +36%, both above guidance
Gen AI sales doubled, faster than GPU shipments
How much of Enterprise comes from a single big customer
How much the long-term deals protect it if data-center building slows
